seo.title: M5.2 Earthquake Strikes Anchorage, USGS Says
seo.description: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake was reported near Anchorage, Alaska, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. USGS assigned a yellow PAGER alert.

paragraphs: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake struck Anchorage, Alaska on Sunday, September 27, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. UTC, the U.S. Geological Survey reported. USGS assigned a yellow PAGER alert level for the event.

body.heading: What USGS reported
paragraphs: The U.S. Geological Survey recorded the earthquake at magnitude 5.2 at a depth of 28.5 kilometers centered near 12 km NNE of Anchorage, Alaska.
USGS listed the event status as "reviewed," indicating that a seismologist had reviewed the automated solution.
USGS assigned the event a significance score of 650.

body.heading: Magnitude and depth
paragraphs: The earthquake had a magnitude of 5.2 on the local magnitude (ML) scale.
The hypocenter was located at a depth of 28.5 kilometers, within the shallow-to-intermediate range typical of crustal activity.

body.heading: Where the earthquake occurred
paragraphs: The epicenter was located near 12 km NNE of Anchorage, Alaska.

body.heading: Felt reports
paragraphs: As of the most recent USGS update, 342 "Did You Feel It?" reports were submitted by residents near the epicenter.
USGS computed a Community Determined Intensity (CDI) of 4.2 from those reports.

body.heading: USGS alert and tsunami information
paragraphs: USGS assigned a yellow (limited impact expected) PAGER alert level for the earthquake through its Prompt Assessment of Global Earthquakes for Response (PAGER) system.
USGS did not flag the event with a tsunami marker.

body.heading: Source
paragraphs: This article was produced from data published by the U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program. The original event page is published by USGS at earthquake.usgs.gov.
